title: FastHarness: Experience-Driven Review Scheduling for Vision-Language-Action Policies
why: A-type agentic robot harness: frozen π0.5 policy under GPT-6 Astra review/recovery. Experience-driven FastHarness adaptively schedules language-model supervision (stage memory + reviewed outcomes reduce review frequency; complementary recovery path repairs then resumes). Directly instantiates execution monitoring/control over a frozen VLA.
mechanism: Execution harness over frozen π0.5: fast path uses stage recognition and outcome memory to skip routine reviews as experience accumulates; recovery path triggers GPT-6 Astra supervision to detect/repair errors then return to routine control. Policy stays frozen and regenerates actions from current observations.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported on four simulated dual-arm manipulation tasks in RoboDojo/Isaac Sim: reviewer tokens −57.2% per task (first episode → mean of last five); mean episode time 85.5→52.0 min; mean success 80% (GPT-as-Policy π0.5+Astra) → 97.19% with FastHarness. Sections 5.1–5.5.
evidence_locator: arXiv abs cs.RO; HTML v1 §4 FastHarness, §5 Experiments (Tables on reviewer use/success), Appendix B setup (Isaac Sim / RoboDojo / two X5 arms)
retrieval_notes: Verified abs + HTML method/experiments. Announced Fri 23 Oct 2026 arXiv /new (cs.RO). GitHub from abs comments. No PDF.

title: Know When to Escalate: Critic-Guided Adaptive Execution for Cloud-Local Embodied Agents
why: A-type cloud–local embodied execution harness (CARE): critic monitors reliability and escalates from a local executor to a stronger cloud model with persistent control until recovery; shared handoff memory preserves task state across transfers. Separates harness routing from fixed planner–executor roles.
mechanism: CARE: high-level planner π_P then dual executors (local π_L = Qwen3.6-35B-A3B; cloud π_C = Claude Sonnet 4.6). Lightweight critic (same Qwen checkpoint, different prompt) triggers escalation when local reliability drops; escalation persists until return threshold; shared handoff memory M_t owned by controller.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported closed-loop on Habitat, EmbodiedBench, and VLABench: SR, E2E latency, time-between-actions, steps, cloud request ratio vs Local-only, Cloud-only, Hi Robot*, RouteLLM*, AdaPlanner. Claims CARE approaches/exceeds Cloud-only success at lower CRR; ablations on handoff memory and critic. §IV.
evidence_locator: arXiv abs cs.RO; HTML v1 §III Method (critic transfer, handoff memory), §IV-A setup (models/benchmarks), §IV-B–D results/ablations
retrieval_notes: Verified abs + HTML. No GitHub on abs. Announced Fri 23 Oct 2026. Exact numeric SR tables not transcribed beyond qualitative claims in §IV headings/abstract-adjacent text.

title: Externalise the Memory: A Pre-Registered Study of Where an Embodied Agent's Experience Should Live
why: A-type harness-memory vs weight-memory study: memory-augmented VLM teacher with external retrieval buffer produces reach trajectories; LoRA students distilled from the same trajectories; re-attaching frozen retrieval to fixed student weights isolates contextual memory. Pre-registered null that experience does not bake into weights.
mechanism: Teacher VLM retrieves lesson cards (text + episode images) from past attempts during a vision-conditioned single-arm reach task; students are LoRA policies distilled from teacher trajectories; evaluation re-attaches the teacher's frozen retrieval buffer to fixed student weights (parametric vs contextual memory on identical weights).
evaluation_signal: Author-reported pre-registered protocols: null that memory bakes into weights (withdrawn underpowered claim); attaching retrieval to fixed student weights +34 pp (z=5.15) toward pooled memory-augmented teacher reference 49.3%; protocol/auto-reset sensitivity contrasts also reported. §4 Results.
evidence_locator: arXiv abs cs.RO (also cs.AI); HTML v1 §3 Methods, §4 Results (T1 null, retrieval reversal), pre-registration appendices; GitHub+pre-registration link on abs
retrieval_notes: Verified abs + HTML. Cross-listed cs.AI. Embodiment is single-arm reach (sim); headline is harness memory attribution rather than a new multi-task agent stack.

title: Alpha: Systematic Fault Injection and Robustness Evaluation for LLM-Driven Embodied Manipulation
why: B-type evaluation harness: systematic fault injection across perception/actuation/kinematics/planning for LLM-driven manipulation, with matched LLM agent vs Scripted Oracle under identical seeds and safety monitor—isolates planner sensitivity from physical vulnerabilities.
mechanism: Alpha fault-injection framework in PyBullet: calibrated faults F1 sensor lag, F2 grip slip, F3 unreachable IK, F4 planner-output corruption (+ concurrent). LLM agent (Llama-3 via Ollama) vs deterministic Scripted Oracle; PyBullet safety monitor at 240 Hz on multi-link contacts.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported balanced 150-episode matrix (75/planner): Oracle 64.0% (48/75) vs LLM 44.0% (33/75), paired McNemar p=3.01e-4; excluding planner corruption, LLM and Oracle match on physical/kinematic/perceptual faults. §IV–V.
evidence_locator: arXiv abs cs.RO; HTML v1 fault taxonomy, matched methodology, results; code URL on abs
retrieval_notes: Verified abs + HTML. Block stacking / tabletop manip in PyBullet DIRECT mode. Announced Fri 23 Oct 2026.

title: Progress Probes P^2: Lightweight Runtime Monitoring for Vision-Language-Action Models
why: B-type runtime verification for VLA deployment: linear probes on π0.5 internal activations estimate task progress and flag off-course executions, competing with external VLM monitors without requiring failure-labeled training data—fits external_verification_control / success-detector family.
mechanism: Train linear progress probes on VLA activations from demonstrations; at runtime compare estimated progress trajectory to expected progress and flag deviations. Contrasts with external VLM judges and failure-classifier monitors (SAFE, Robometer).
evaluation_signal: Author-reported sim + real (Franka Research 3, DROID cameras; π0.5 / π0.5-DROID finetuned on 6 hardware tasks × 60 demos): AUROC ~0.788/0.78 matching or exceeding SAFE and Robometer; competitive with VLM monitors; hardware failure detection and unseen-task generalization in §VI–VII.
evidence_locator: arXiv abs cs.RO; HTML v1 §V method, §VI simulation, §VII hardware
retrieval_notes: Verified abs + HTML. No GitHub on abs. Pure monitoring (not a full agent loop) but in-scope as verification component for harnessed VLA deployment.

title: CMAR-search: Commonsense and Memory Augmented Reasoning for Object Search in Dynamic Interactive Environments
why: A-type LLM-driven mobile-manipulation search agent: builds a Functional 3D Scene Graph with commonsense area labels and environmental memory, then hierarchical LLM planning for interactive object search (open containers, relocate) in dynamic scenes—harness memory + planner over an embodied Fetch robot.
mechanism: CMAR: LLM interaction constructs/optimizes Functional 3DSG (area functionalities + memory); hierarchical action planning with prompt-constrained area inspection and A* proximity; dynamic-environment response heuristics for object relocation. Macro plans decompose into container-inspection micro-steps.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported iGibson Fetch sim (8 train / 7 test scenes) plus real-world experiments: vs MoMa-LLM and other baselines, e.g. +24.2% SPL (competitive SR) and larger SR/SPL gains on NTS/TR task splits (43.3%/35.8% and 17.1%/17.8% cited vs one baseline). §IV-B/C.
evidence_locator: arXiv abs cs.RO; HTML v1 §III method (F3DSG, hierarchical planning), §IV sim/real; ICRA 2026
retrieval_notes: Verified abs + HTML. Specific LLM checkpoint name for planning not stated in read sections (prompts/figures referenced); GPT-4 only acknowledged for manuscript polishing. No GitHub on abs.

title: SCOPE: Scene-graph Construction Optimized by Plan Error-correction for Robot Long-term Planning Datasets
why: B-type dataset/tooling for LLM TAMP: SCOPE generates diverse scene graphs + CoT task instructions, then plan generation with error-correction to produce fine-tuning data; LoRA-tuned Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct plans execute in AI2-THOR—supports harnessed LLM planners rather than a pure VLA.
mechanism: Pipeline: statistical-feedback scene-graph sampling → CoT task instruction generation → plan generation with error-correction → LoRA fine-tune of Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct; closed-loop execution of emitted plan sequences in AI2-THOR.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported planning robustness under erroneous data and fine-tuning ablations (scene diversity / error-correction); LoRA student claims higher success than counterpart fine-tuned on DELTA (PDDL planner) data. Project page linked. §IV.
evidence_locator: arXiv abs cs.RO; HTML v1 §III pipeline, §IV experiments; project https://scope-page.github.io/; IROS 2026
retrieval_notes: Verified abs + HTML. B-type dataset/generator for LLM planners; not a novel deployment harness loop. Exact numeric success deltas beyond 'higher than DELTA-data counterpart' not fully transcribed from tables.

title: Multi-Tool Selection for Robotic Systems: Comparing Semantic Retrieval and LLM
why: B-type robot tool-routing study: selects the minimal complete subset of predefined executable robot capabilities for natural-language commands, comparing ChromaDB retrieval variants vs a 120B LLM baseline—directly about the tool-exposure layer of an embodied harness.
mechanism: Offline tool routing for compound NL robot requests: CDB-v1 fixed-threshold, CDB-v2 relative-distance, CDB-v3 clause-aware aggregated ChromaDB retrieval vs cloud 120B LLM. Metrics: exact-match accuracy, completeness, precision, completeness-weighted composite, latency.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported on 164 manually annotated prompts (3 complexity levels). CDB-v3 best retrieval-only macro-average composite 0.7822 vs LLM baseline 0.8869; LLM higher routing quality at higher latency. §5. No closed-loop task success in a simulator claimed in read sections.
evidence_locator: arXiv abs cs.RO (also cs.AI); HTML v1 §4 strategies, §5 results
retrieval_notes: Verified abs + HTML. Evaluation is label-matching on prompts, not online robot episodes—still in scope as harness tool-selection component. No GitHub on abs.
